UPSTREAM: mac80211: mac80211: Check SN for deactivated mpaths When processing a PREQ or PREP it's critical to use the incoming SN. If that is improperly done routing loops and other types of badness can happen. But the code was always processing path messages for deactivated paths. This path fixes that so that if we have a valid SN then we use it to verify that it is a message we can accept. For reference the relevant section of the standard is 13.10.8.4 which doesn't address the deactivated path case at all. I also included a special case for when our peer reboots or restarts networking. This is an important case because without it there can be a very long delay before we accept path messages from that peer. It's also a simple case and intimately associated with processing messages for deactivated paths so I used one patch instead of two. (cherry picked from commit "d8f0300a7aca5cd9208112104c64d894ad82da1f") (source: git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/ath.git) BUG=chrome-os-partner:49352 TEST=build/boot on Arkham and verified iperf throughput. Change-Id: I55dde29a634e899c37641379da7cc35aa489e4cb Signed-off-by: Alexis Green <agreen@cococorp.com> Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/322375 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Peter Oh <poh@qca.qualcomm.com> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: mac80211: mesh: fix call_rcu() usage When using call_rcu(), the called function may be delayed quite significantly, and without a matching rcu_barrier() there's no way to be sure it has finished. Therefore, global state that could be gone/freed/reused should never be touched in the callback. Fix this in mesh by moving the atomic_dec() into the caller; that's not really a problem since we already unlinked the path and it will be destroyed anyway. This fixes a crash Jouni observed when running certain tests in a certain order, in which the mesh interface was torn down, the memory reused for a function pointer (work struct) and running that then crashed since the pointer had been decremented by 1, resulting in an invalid instruction byte stream. (cherry picked from commit "c2e703a55245bfff3db53b1f7cbe59f1ee8a4339") (source: git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/ath.git) BUG=chrome-os-partner:49352 TEST=build/boot on Arkham and verified iperf throughput. CHROMIUM: alt-syscall: Whitelist additional I/O syscalls Whitelist some additional I/O syscalls which may be used by Android.
